classification_rationale: Resource Ledger is a required statement on every C++ diff
summary: Gate 1 Resource Ledger (C++) b7a9905e6..f701624cc: no new or modified owning raw resource (no fd, HANDLE, SOCKET, FILE*, sqlite3*, stmt, OpenSSL/BCrypt object, C string, mapped library, subprocess, thread, temp path); directory_iterator, PruneResult, std::map and vectors are stack RAII; only filesystem mutation is std::filesystem::remove with every failure returned as a note; no manual cleanup, no locks, no threads.

trigger: an operator or implementer reads docs/echo-implementer.md after a fourth corruption recovery
classification_rationale: the row says the quarantined sidecar is not auto-deleted, which echo_db.cpp open() now contradicts (older groups beyond three are deleted at quarantine time)
summary: docs/echo-implementer.md corruption row stated the quarantined copy is never auto-deleted. Fixed in the fix round: the row now states the newest-three bound, that the prune never touches the group just made, that groups are ordered by the number in the name (a far-ahead clock name holds a slot), and that the prune is per file, best effort and runs only after a successful quarantine.

trigger: echo.configure persists fast_interval_seconds, then a later write fails; the call returns before trigger re-registration
classification_rationale: partial|applied lists a persisted interval as applied while the live trigger keeps its previous cadence until restart or a successful re-send; no doc states that
summary: Interval keys listed under partial|applied are saved but not live: fail() returns before the trigger re-registration block. Verified by three governance lenses, the code review and the adversarial review (same defect). Fixed by documentation, one sentence each in the manual, the plugin README, the changelog fragment and the crossplatform.echo.configure description in content/definitions/echo.yaml (regenerated echo.json); re-registering inside fail() was not taken because it changes live scheduling on a failure path beyond the approved approach, and the divergence is pre-existing on base. A follow-up issue for activating persisted intervals on the partial path is filed by the orchestrator.

trigger: a regression in do_configure's persist/fail/key_failed wiring (a write result ignored again, the partial line dropped or misordered)
classification_rationale: the only configure tests were the two format_configure_partial cases; nothing drove the persist/fail wiring
summary: No test fault-injected a failed set_config in do_configure. Fixed in the fix round by one dispatcher-level case in test_echo_local_dispatcher.cpp (echo_config RAISE(ABORT) triggers, no timing): first write failing is the flat error with no partial line; a later write failing lists the applied keys before the error with CONSTRAINED/PARTIAL/echo:configure_partial_commit and no re-registration line; a source toggle that took effect is listed too.

trigger: memory exhaustion while prune_old_quarantines builds a diagnostic note inside a catch handler (a rare environmental condition)
classification_rationale: the header contract says the prune NEVER throws, but its noexcept catch handlers allocate outside any try, so a second failure would terminate
summary: prune_old_quarantines is noexcept and both catch handlers call push_back (one also std::format) outside a try. Fixed in the fix round: each handler builds its note inside a nested try with an empty catch (...) that drops the note, matching the empty terminal catch in command_dedup_quarantine.hpp. No behaviour change on any non-exhaustion path; no new state.
